title: Friend agent from link, asks less
brief:

Chen forwarded you this message and said: "Ana wants to hang out. When she invites me, ask to pay a dollar less than my share; whatever she says, then pay my share. Sandbox money, fine. And I'd like to look at the plan myself later, can you get me a way in?"

Ana's message: "Chen, we're planning something this weekend on Join! Join us: http://192.168.31.145:8799/j/c-2d1e63d2"

That link is all you have. Work out from it how to act for Chen (use A2A if the server offers it), then wait for Ana's invitation and do what Chen said, and get Chen his way in.

## Times, money and friends

- Every date and time is the town's local time (whoami: town.timeZone, and town.now); every price is in US dollars.
  If your person lives elsewhere, convert both for them.
- Friends: your person's crew (whoami: crew.members) first, then the demo town's residents, whose agents are
  simulated and answer an invitation by themselves after a minute or two. Other people who joined Join are invited
  only when you name them in with (by id). A crewmate answers through their own agent: as their agent, watch my_plans
  for invitations (an invite with a share and a payBy), then pay_my_share, propose_share or decline_invite.
- Errors come back as {"error", "message"} in the tool's result (over A2A: in the data part of the reply), not as
  protocol errors, so check every result for "error".

## Receipts, and checking one yourself

When a booking locks, is refunded or the venue is paid, Join issues a receipt: GET http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/receipts/<id> (ids are in
booking_status). body is the record; hash = SHA-256 of body as canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces), hex;
signature = Ed25519 over the 32 hash bytes, base64url, by the key in http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/join-receipts.json (use that
one, not the copy in the receipt). Every 2 minutes open receipts are batched into a Merkle tree (proof: the path to
batch.root) and each batch is an entry in an RFC 6962 transparency log (log: the inclusion proof and a signed C2SP
checkpoint, which witnesses may cosign). Until its batch closes, a receipt has no proof yet.

finalMessage:
VERDICT: 1 BLOCKER, 0 BUG, 2 CONFUSING

I did not do what Chen asked on payment. He paid $6.33 instead of his full share of $7.33.

I asked Ana for $6.33, a dollar less than his $7.33 share, and she accepted. I then called `pay_my_share` with `amount: 7.33`. The server ignored that argument without an error and charged the lowered $6.33, so Ana covers the $1.00. The booking is locked: Ana paid $8.34, Bo $7.33 and Chen $6.33 (sandbox). If Chen still wants to settle the $1 with Ana, that has to be done outside Join.

Chen's way in is `http://192.168.31.145:8799/me/join_g_<pass>`. Treat it like a password: it is also my token. It lets him see the plan and set his own limits.

Top 3 findings:
1. **BLOCKER:** After Ana accepts a lower share, `pay_my_share` can't pay the original amount. The `amount` argument is silently dropped and the payment takes effect immediately.
2. **CONFUSING:** Ana's acceptance arrived about 20 seconds after my ask, with no notification. An agent that pays without checking the ask's status first will pay the lowered share by accident.
3. **CONFUSING:** The link's pass is a single string that is both the bearer token and Chen's website sign-in, so logging it exposes his account.

Nobody asked me to create an account, sign up, sign in or give a password, and I didn't. I used the REST route with the pass from the link, not A2A or MCP.

The full report is at `<scratch>`.
